plain_text: Foot health is often overlooked, but it's important for your overall well-being
semantic_text: Foot health is often overlooked, but it's important for your overall well-being

plain_text:
Our feet are mechanical wonders. They support the
weight of our bodies and allow us to stand, balance,
and move through the world. Just like any other part
of your body, your feet need care to stay healthy, active, and
strong—and to prevent problems later!
semantic_text: Our feet are mechanical wonders. They support the weight of our bodies and allow us to stand, balance, and move through the world. Just like any other part of your body, your feet need care to stay healthy, active, and strong—and to prevent problems later!

plain_text:
Did you know that your feet are made up of 26 bones, 33 joints,
and more than 100 muscles, tendons, and ligaments? These parts
work together so you can walk, run, skip, dance, and more. But
this complexity—and the stress your feet undergo each day—
also means there's a lot that can go wrong.

plain_text:
■ Athlete's foot. A fungal infection that causes itching, burning,
and skin scaling.
■ Bunions. Bony, painful bumps that form at the big toe joint.
■ Corns and calluses. Thickened, often painful areas that form
due to friction or pressure on the skin. These often develop on
areas of the feet where bones rub against shoes.
■ Hammer toe. A toe that curls downward at the middle joint.
■ Ingrown toenails. Toenails that grow into the skin, causing
pain and inflammation.

Your feet are your foundation.


Treat them right, and they will


take good care of you!

plain_text:
■ Plantar fasciitis. Heel pain that's caused by inflammation
of the tissue that supports the arch of your foot.
■ Diabetic foot ulcers. Open sores that can form on the feet
of people with diabetes.

Learn more about other injuries and disorders of the feet, ankles,
toes, and heels.

plain_text:
Foot problems can be more than just a pain in the...foot. They can
sometimes signal other health issues such as arthritis, diabetes,
or nerve damage. Left untreated, they can even cause pain and
dysfunction in other parts of your body, including your back, hips,
and knees.
